segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Soon afterward he went traveling through town and village, proclaiming and announcing the good news of the kingdom of God. The Twelve were with him,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and also some women who had been healed of evil spirits and illnesses: Mary, the one called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others, who were providing for them out of their own means.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As a large crowd was gathering and people from town after town were making their way to him, he spoke by means of a parable:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The sower went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell along the path and was trampled, and the birds of the sky ate it up.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Other seed fell on the rock, and when it sprouted it withered, because it had no moisture.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Other seed fell in the middle of the thorns, and the thorns sprouted along with it and choked it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And other seed fell into the good soil, and when it sprouted it produced fruit a hundredfold.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he said these things he called out,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His disciples asked him what this parable meant.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “To you it has been given to know the secrets of the kingdom of God, but to the rest it comes in parables, so that seeing they may not see, and hearing they may not understand.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Now this is what the parable means: the seed is the word of God.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Those along the path are the ones who have heard; then the devil comes and takes away the word from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Those on the rock are the ones who, when they hear, receive the word with joy. But these have no root; they believe for a time, and in a time of testing they fall away.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: As for what fell into the thorns, these are the ones who have heard, but as they go on their way they are choked by the worries and wealth and pleasures of life, and they bring no fruit to maturity.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But as for what is in the fine soil, these are the ones who, having heard the word with a fine and good heart, hold on to it and bear fruit with endurance.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: No one lights a lamp and then covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed. Instead, he puts it on a lampstand, so that those who come in may see the light.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For nothing is hidden that will not be brought into the open, and nothing concealed that will not be known and come into the open.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So take care how you listen. For to whoever has, more will be given; and from whoever does not have, even what they think they have will be taken away.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: His mother and his brothers came to him, but they could not reach him because of the crowd.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He was told,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My mother and my brothers are these: the ones who hear the word of God and do it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One day he got into a boat with his disciples, and he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Let us cross to the other side of the lake.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So they put out.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As they sailed he fell asleep. A windstorm came down on the lake, and they were being swamped and were in danger.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came and woke him, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Master, Master, we are perishing!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He woke and rebuked the wind and the surging water; they stopped, and there was a calm.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Where is your faith?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Afraid and amazed, they said to one another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Who then is this, that he gives orders even to the winds and the water, and they obey him?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came to land in the country of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he stepped out onto the land, a man from the town who had demons met him. For a long time he had worn no clothing, and he did not live in a house but among the tombs.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he saw Jesus, he cried out, fell down before him, and said in a loud voice,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What do you want with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: For Jesus had been commanding the unclean spirit to come out of the man. Many times it had seized him; he would be bound with chains and shackles and kept under guard, but he would break the bonds and be driven by the demon into the deserted places.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus asked him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What is your name?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Legion,”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: because many demons had entered him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they kept pleading with him not to order them to go away into the abyss.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now a large herd of pigs was feeding there on the hillside, and they pleaded with him to permit them to enter those. He permitted them.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The demons came out of the man and entered the pigs, and the herd rushed down the steep bank into the lake and drowned.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the herdsmen saw what had happened, they fled and told it in the town and in the countryside.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: People went out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed and in his right mind, and they were afraid.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Those who had seen it told them how the man who had been possessed by demons was saved.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the whole population of the surrounding region of the Gerasenes asked him to go away from them, because they were gripped by great fear. So he got into a boat and returned.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The man from whom the demons had gone out begged to be with him, but Jesus sent him away, saying,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Return to your home, and recount all that God has done for you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he went away, proclaiming throughout the whole town all that Jesus had done for him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, for they were all expecting him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Just then a man named Jairus came, a leader of the synagogue. Falling at the feet of Jesus, he pleaded with him to come to his house,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: because he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, and she was dying. As Jesus went, the crowds were smothering him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years, and who, though she had spent her whole livelihood on physicians, could not be healed by anyone,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: came up behind him and touched the tassel of his cloak, and at once her flow of blood stopped.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Who is it that touched me?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When everyone denied it, Peter said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Master, the crowds are hemming you in and pressing against you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Someone touched me, for I knew that power had gone out from me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the woman saw that she had not escaped notice, she came trembling, fell down before him, and told before all the people why she had touched him and how she had been cured at once.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While he was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue leader’s house and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Your daughter has died. Do not trouble the teacher any longer.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus heard this and answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do not be afraid. Only believe, and she will be saved.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he came to the house, he did not allow anyone to go in with him except Peter, John, and James, and the child’s father and mother.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Everyone was weeping and mourning for her. But he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do not weep, for she has not died but is sleeping.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they laughed at him, knowing that she had died.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he took hold of her hand and called out,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Child, get up!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Her spirit came back, and she stood up at once, and he directed that she be given something to eat.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Her parents were astounded, but he commanded them to tell no one what had happened.

notes.note: The Herod meant here is Herod Antipas, son of Herod the Great and ruler of Galilee during Jesus’ ministry. The Greek word covers a manager of a household or estate; Chuza’s exact office is not known, but Joanna evidently belonged to court circles and had money of her own.

The Greek word is the one usually translated ‘heaven’, here in its ordinary sense of the visible sky. The traditional ‘birds of the air’ is an English idiom; ‘sky’ is what the word means in this phrase.

notes.traditional: that seeing they might not see
notes.note: The words echo Isaiah 6:9–10, where the prophet is sent to a people who will hear without understanding. The Greek conjunction normally expresses purpose, and it is translated that way here. Some interpreters take it as expressing result, or as shorthand for ‘so that the scripture is fulfilled’; the parallel in Matthew 13:13 has ‘because’.

The older English tradition has ‘temptation’, which now suggests enticement to sin. In the usage of the period, including the Greek Old Testament, the word covers any trial that puts loyalty to the proof, and the parallel accounts speak of trouble and persecution. Many modern versions also have ‘testing’ here.

Luke pairs two Greek words for ‘good’ that together formed a stock phrase in Greek for a person of sound and admirable character. The first is the same word used of the soil earlier in the verse, so ‘fine’ is used for both to keep the link. The parallel accounts in Matthew and Mark do not have the phrase.

Manuscripts are divided here and in verse 37 between Gerasenes, Gadarenes and Gergesenes, and the same variation occurs in the parallel accounts. Gerasa was a city more than thirty miles from the lake and Gadara a few miles from it, which probably prompted the changes. SBLGNT reads Gerasenes; the older English tradition has Gadarenes.

The Greek phrase can mean either ‘on many occasions’ or ‘for a long time’. The first is chosen because the sentence goes on to describe repeated binding and escape, but the second is equally possible grammatically.

A Latin military term taken into Greek. A Roman legion at full strength numbered roughly five to six thousand soldiers, so the name signals a vast number and would have carried overtones of an occupying force.

In the Greek Old Testament the word is used for the primeval deep. In Jewish writing of the period it had also come to mean a place where rebellious spirits are confined, a sense also found in Revelation. The parallel in Mark 5:10 has the demons ask not to be sent out of the region.

Most translations have ‘healed’ here and ‘made you well’ in verses 48 and 50, but ‘saved’ in verse 12. Luke uses one verb throughout, which covered rescue from danger, disease and death as well as salvation in the religious sense. Verse 48 also repeats word for word what Jesus says to the forgiven woman in 7:50. One English word is kept so the reader can see the connection Luke’s first readers would have heard.

notes.phrase: though she had spent her whole livelihood on physicians
notes.traditional: which had spent all her living upon physicians
notes.note: These words are missing from some early and important manuscripts, and some editions bracket them and some translations omit them. SBLGNT prints them as part of the text. A similar statement stands without dispute in Mark 5:26.

Traditional renderings are ‘hem’, ‘border’, ‘fringe’ or ‘edge’, and the word can mean simply the edge of a garment. In the Greek Old Testament it is the term for the tassels Israelite men were commanded to wear on the corners of their garments (Numbers 15:38–39). That is probably what a first-century reader would picture on a Jewish teacher’s cloak, though the plainer sense cannot be ruled out.

candidates.reason: The verb covers healing, rescue and salvation, and translations switch between ‘heal’, ‘make well’ and ‘save’ in ways that hide deliberate echoes such as Luke 7:50 and 8:48.
The choice between ‘temptation’, ‘testing’ and ‘trial’ recurs across the Gospels, the letters and Revelation, including the Lord’s Prayer, and should be settled once.
Traditional ‘patience’ now suggests passive waiting; the word recurs in Paul, Hebrews, James and Revelation, where translators vary between endurance, perseverance and steadfastness.
‘Mystery’ suggests a puzzle in modern English, whereas the word means something hidden and now disclosed; it recurs in the Gospels, Paul and Revelation and needs one policy.
This form of address is peculiar to Luke and needs to be kept distinct from the renderings chosen for κύριος, διδάσκαλος and ῥαββί.
